evidence:
Inventory of every universal/plural/exactly-N wording and every 'unchanged / nothing changes' guard in the 47 criteria (2 gate, 40 functional, 5 polish; visual is read-only Likert).

WHOLE-COLLECTION CHECKS THAT ARE CORRECT: hro_bulk_move ('Fails if ... only some move'), hro_bulk_all_or_none ('none of the set moves', UI and replay), hro_bulk_places ('none moves'; 'Interview places are counted for the whole set' per hireops_rules.md:91-92), hro_undo_restores (W, X and Y each checked, V checked to stay), hro_thread_earlier ('until none remain'), hro_thread_latest (whole 30-message window), hro_activity filter clause ('shows all of that job's lines and only those'), hro_activity_refusals ('none of the refused attempts in this review added a line'), hro_candidate_private plus protocol K ('Capture every request the candidate page makes and inspect every response', functional/prompt.md:43), hro_candidate_view ('only their own applications' over the full list; Noor has two seeded applications APP-101/APP-302 so 'only' is non-trivially exercised), hro_restart (jobs, order per stage, notes, messages and activity all compared), gate hro_gate_shared ('exactly one card ... in Applied', catches double-insert).

EXACTLY-N COUNTS: hro_unread_counts ('rises by exactly two and his total by two') and hro_unread_scrolled_up ('told there is one new message'). Legitimate concurrent side effects cannot inflate them: test.sh:207 runs rewardkit with '--max-concurrent-agent 1', so polish's Noor messages cannot land during functional protocol U; the count is phrased as a delta and functional/prompt.md:19 says 'Record before/after facts per row', which covers the non-zero baseline Rafael may have from Mei's and Bill's T-protocol messages.

'UNCHANGED' GUARDS: functional/prompt.md:19 explicitly allows legitimate side effects ('A refused action may add a generic log line but must not change any card, order, message, note or activity entry'); hro_pol_live_board says scroll 'has not been reset' (not 'unchanged', so a shift caused by the moved card is tolerated); hro_pol_earlier_place tolerates 'within a few pixels'; hro_pol_live_thread fails only if the view 'moves away from the newest message', so appending the arrival is allowed; hro_stale_refused, hro_undo_conflict, hro_undo_full, hro_interview_full, hro_reject_hired, hro_mgr_* and hro_observer_readonly guard only the refused operation's own records while the matching success is the control. No guard punishes a side effect of the operation it grades.

DEFECT (the one instance where a universal requirement is graded on a sample): hireops_rules.md:110 says 'Every job opening, added candidate, move, rejection, reopening, re-ordering and undo is recorded with who did it and what changed'. hro_activity (functional/judge.toml:257-264) only asks that the view 'lists opening, adding, moves, rejection with its reason, reopening, re-ordering and undo' and its fail clause is 'Fails if any of these kinds is missing, unattributed, out of order, or the filter drops or mixes lines'; protocol A (functional/prompt.md:49) likewise asks for 'lines for opening, adding, moving, ... and undoing'. One line of each kind satisfies it, so the 'every' ask is checked by kind, not across the actions the review actually performed. The multi-card move (/api/moves/bulk in the golden, index.js:327) and its undo are a separate code path that the brief stresses, and protocol B performs them on J2, yet nothing requires their lines to be present.

LOWER-RISK NOTES (no verdict change on their own): (a) hro_pol_failed_send pass bar 'nothing was added to the conversation' could be read against a conforming 'not sent - retry' local bubble, though its fail clause ('lost, shown as sent, or sent twice') does not punish it; brief only requires the text to stay in the box (hireops_rules.md:139-140). (b) hro_candidate_view says 'each candidate' while protocol K signs in only Noor and Tomas (Lena only at Z); a judge can read 'each' as the candidates exercised, so no conforming app is penalised. (c) hro_activity_refusals pass text 'added a line' vs prompt:19 'may add a generic log line' and brief hireops_rules.md:113 'A refused action adds no entry' are slightly inconsistent but resolve leniently via the fail clause 'appears as if it happened'.

OUT-OF-ROW OBSERVATIONS FOR THE OWNER (not graded under #31; for rows 30/32 reviewers to confirm independently): (i) protocol B steps (9)-(11) / hro_undo_once second leg: Mei has already moved X in step 9, so the step-11 replay of the V-and-X undo is refused for the conflict regardless of whether the app enforces 'an earlier move is no longer undoable once the same person has made a later one'; that leg cannot discriminate. (ii) hro_observer_readonly / hro_candidate_no_staff replay Rafael's observed move and add-candidate requests unchanged; a stale version (409) or duplicate email would refuse them without any role check, so only the note and open-job legs actually prove role enforcement.

No configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index.json scope: scripted golden observations only), so the finding is a design finding, not a run-confirmed one.
counterexample: Broken app: activity is written inside the single-card move/reject/reopen/reorder/undo handlers but the multi-card move handler and the undo of a multi-card move write no activity line (a separately coded bulk route). On the functional run, protocol A sees single moves on J1 and V's single move/undo on J2, so every listed kind (opening, adding, moves, rejection with reason, reopening, re-ordering, undo) is present, attributed and newest first, and the J2 filter shows all lines that exist. hro_activity scores 1 although the brief's 'Every ... move ... and undo is recorded' is violated for the three-card moves and their undo in protocol B. Similarly an app that drops activity for hiring-manager moves (protocol R) would pass.
suggested_fix: Make hro_activity and protocol A check instances, not kinds: e.g. 'every successful action you performed on J1 and J2 has its line, including each card of the three-card moves in B and the undo of that move, and Ingrid's moves in R', and fail if any performed action has no line.
